strepo.definition: strepō uī, —, ere, to make a noise, rattle, rustle, rumble, murmur, hum, roar: Inter se, C. poët.: fluvii-strepunt Hibernā nive turgidi, H.: strepit adsiduo cava tempora circum Tinnitu galea, V.: haec cum streperent, …

strictim.definition: strictim adv. strictus, superficially, cursorily, summarily, briefly : quasi per transennam strictim aspicere: dici (opp. copiosissime): dicere.

strictura.definition: strictūra ae, f STRAG-, a compression ; hence, a mass of metal under the forge : striduntque cavernis Stricturae Chalybum, V.

strictus.definition: strictus adj. P. of stringo, drawn together, close, strait, tight : nodus, L.: artūs, Ta.

strideo.definition: strīdeō —, —, ēre, to make a harsh noise, hiss, whiz: ferrum igne rubens Stridet in undā, O.: presso molari, gnash, Iu.

strido.definition: strīdō —, —, ere, to make a shrill noise, sound harshly, creak, hiss, grate, whiz, whistle, rattle, buzz: stridentia tinguunt Aera lacu, V.: cruor stridit, hisses, O.: belua Lernae Horrendum stridens, V.: horrendā noc…

stridor.definition: strīdor ōris, m strido, a harsh noise, shrill sound, creak, grating, hiss, rattle, buzz : (serpentis), O.: (elephantorum), L.: Aquilonis: rudentum, V.: ianuae, O.: catenae, Iu.: acutus, H.: indignatum magnis stridorib…

stridulus.definition: strīdulus adj. strido, creaking, rattling, hissing, whizzing, buzzing : cornus (i. e. hasta), V.: Fax fumo, O.

strigilis.definition: strigilis is (plur abl. striglibus, Iu.), f STRAG-, a scraper, strigil (of horn or metal, for bathers), C., H., Iu.

strigosus.definition: (strigōsus) adj. STRAG-, lean, lank, thin, meagre .— Only comp: strigosiores equi, i. e. worn out , L.—Fig., of an orator: strigosior, too meagre .

stringo.definition: stringō inxī, ictus, ere STRAG-, to draw tight, bind tight, compress, press together : stricta frigore volnera, L.: ferri duritiem, forge , Ct. dub.— To touch lightly, graze : laevas cautes, V.: Stringebat summas ales…

strix.definition: strix strigis, f , stri/gc, a screech-owl (superstitiously regarded as a vampire or harpy): volucres . . . Est illis strigibus nomen, O.: strigis infames alae (used in incantations), O.

stropha.definition: stropha ae, f , strofh/, a trick, artifice, Ph.

strophium.definition: strophium ī, n , stro/fion, a breast-band, stay, C., Ct.

structor.definition: strūctor ōris, m STRV-, a builder, mason, carpenter : res agebatur multis structoribus.— A server, carver , Iu.

structura.definition: strūctūra ae, f STRV-, a building, mode of building, construction : parietum, Cs.: structurae antiquae genus, L.: aerariae structurae, i. e. mines , Cs.—Fig., of language, an arrangement, order, structure : mei carmin…

strues.definition: struēs is, f STRV-, a heap, pile : laterum: lignorum, L.: Arma cum telis in strue mixta, O.: rogi, a funeral pile , Ta.: (milites) confusā strue implicantur, a mass (the phalanx), L.— A heap of little sacrificial cake…

struma.definition: strūma ae, f STRV-, a scrofulous tumor, swollen gland, struma : Vatini: civitatis.

strumosus.definition: strūmōsus adj. struma, having a struma, scrofulous, strumous : homo, Iu.

struo.definition: struō strūxī, strūctus, ere STRV-, to place together, heap up, pile, arrange : quasi structa et nexa verbis, etc.: lateres, qui super musculo struantur, Cs.: ad sidera montī s, O.: ordine longam penum, V.: altaria don…

studeo.definition: studeō uī, —, ēre, to give attention, be eager, be zealous, take pains, be diligent, be busy with, be devoted, strive after, apply oneself, pursue, desire, wish: ut aequum fuerat atque ut studui, T.: nihil egregie, T.…

studiose.definition: studiōsē adv. with comp. and sup. studiosus, eagerly, zealously, anxiously, carefully, studiously, devotedly : Texentem telam studiose offendimus, T.: pila ludere: discere: ego cum antea studiose commendabam Marcilium…

studiosus.definition: studiōsus adj. with comp. and sup. studium, eager, zealous, assiduous, anxious, fond, studious : homo: venandi aut pilae: placendi, O.: culinae, H.: summe omnium doctrinarum: restituendi mei quam retinendi studiosior.…

studium.definition: studium ī, n cf. studeo, application, assiduity, zeal, eagerness, fondness, inclination, desire, exertion, endeavor, study : illum summo cum studio servare: studium semper adsit, cunctatio absit: non studio accusare, …

stulte.definition: stultē adv. with comp. and sup. stultus, foolishly, sillily, stupidly : Factum a nobis stultest, T.: haud stulte sapis, you are no fool , T.: stultius illum quam se duxisse, L.: multa improbe fecisti, unum stultissime.

stultitia.definition: stultitia ae, f stultus, folly, foolishness, simplicity, silliness, fatuity : stultitiā facere, T.: non omnis error stultitia dicenda est: stultitiā ac temeritate vestrā Galliam prosternere, Cs.: cuius ea stultitia es…

stultus.definition: stultus adj. with comp. and sup. 1 STAR-, foolish, simple, silly, fatuous, stupid, dull : Quae sunt dicta in stulto, caudex, etc., T.: Camilli: civitas: adrogantia, Cs.: laetitia, S.: levitas, Ph.: consilium stultissi…

stupefacio.definition: stupefaciō fēcī, factus, ere stupeo+facio, to make stupid, strike senseless, benumb, stun, stupefy : privatos luctūs stupefecit publicus pavor, i. e. overwhelmed , L.: quem stupefacti dicentem intuenter? dumb with ama…

stupens.definition: stupēns ntis, adj. P. of stupeo, senseless, benumbed, stiff, numb : membra, Cu.: volnus, Cu.— Fig., dumb, astounded, amazed, dazed, confused : quae cum intuerer stupens: vigiles attoniti et stupentibus similes, Cu.: t…

stupeo.definition: stupeō uī, ēre STIP-, to be struck senseless, be stunned, be benumbed, be aghast, be astounded, be amazed, be stupefied : animus stupet, T.: cum hic semisomnus stuperet: exspectatione, L.: aere, H.: in titulis, H.: in…

stupesco.definition: stupēscō —, —, ere, inch. stupeo, to grow astonished, become amazed .

stupiditas.definition: stupiditās ātis, f stupidus, senselessness, dulness, stupidity : hominis.

stupidus.definition: stupidus adj. STIP-, senseless, confounded, amazed : tabula te stupidum detinet: populus studio, T.— Senseless, dull, stupid, foolish, stolid : stupidum esse Socratem dixit: Corinthus, Iu.

stupor.definition: stupor ōris, m STIP-, numbness, dulness, insensibility, stupor : in corpore: sensus: stupor obstitit illis (lacrimis), O.: stupor omnium animos tenet, L.: linguae.— Astonishment, amazement : tantus te stupor oppressit…

stuppa.definition: stūppa or stūpa ae, f , stu/ph, coarse flax, tow, oakum: (telum) stuppā circumligabant, L., Cs., V.

stuppeus.definition: stūppeus or stūpeus adj. stuppa, of tow, flaxen : vincula, V.: retinacula, O.: flamma, i. e. burning tow , V.

stupro.definition: stuprō āvī, ātus, āre stuprum, to defile : pulvinar.— To debauch, deflour, ravish, violate : ne stupraretur (filia): stuprata mater familiae, L.

stuprum.definition: stuprum ī, n defilement, dishonor, disgrace, violation, outrage, incest, lust : coniugem inlexe in stuprum: nefarium: hinc pudicitia (pugnat), illinc stuprum: cum sorore stuprum fecisse: cum Fulviā stupri consuetudo, …

suadeo.definition: suādeō sī, sus, ēre SVAD-, to advise, recommend, exhort, urge, persuade : non iubeo, sed suadeo: recte, T.: ita faciam, ut suades: an C. Trebonio persuasi? cui ne suadere quidem ausus essem: coepi suadere pacem: digit…

suasio.definition: suāsiō ōnis, f SVAD-, a recommending, advocacy, support : legis Serviliae.—In rhet., a hortatory address, persuasive speaking : praecepta de suasionibus.

suasor.definition: suāsor ōris, m SVAD-, an exhorter, adviser, counsellor, persuader : repudiatis malis suasoribus: facti: pacis, O.— Of an enactment, a proposer, advocate : non suasor sed regator.

suasus2.definition: suāsus ūs, m an advising, persuading: ob meum suasum, T.

suave.definition: suāvē adv. suavis, sweetly, agreeably, pleasantly : resonare, H.: rubens, V.: olens, Ct.

suaviloquens.definition: suāviloquēns entis, adj. suave+loquens, sweet-spoken, speaking agreeably : os, Enn. ap. C.

suaviloquentia.definition: suāviloquentia ae, f suaviloquens, sweetness of speech, agreeableness .

suavior.definition: suāvior or sāvior —, ārī, dep. suavium, to kiss : Atticam: os, oculosque, Ct.

suavis.definition: suāvis e, adj. with comp. and sup. SVAD-.— To the senses, sweet, agreeable, grateful : odor: res, H.: anima, Ph.—Fig., to the mind, pleasant, agreeable, grateful, attractive, gratifying : homo, T.: homines: sermo Suav…

suavitas.definition: suāvitās ātis, f suavis.—To the senses, sweetness, pleasantness, agreeableness : piscium: odorum: villa mirificā suavitate: conquirere suavitates.—Fig., to the mind, pleasantness, agreeableness, attractiveness : mira …

suaviter.definition: suāviter adv. with comp. and sup. suavis.— To the senses, sweetly, pleasantly, delightfully : sensibus blandiri: dicere.— Fig., to the mind, agreeably, attractively, delightfully, pleasantly : secunda meminisse: suavi…

suavium.definition: suāvium ī, n a kiss; see savium.

sub.definition: sub (in composition sometimes sus- or sū-), praep. with acc. and abl. I. With abl., of position in space, under, below, beneath, underneath, behind : sub terrā habitare: cultrum sub veste abditum habere, L.: sub pelli…

subabsurde.definition: subabsurdē adv. subabsurdus, somewhat absurdly : quae subabsurde salseque dicuntur, i. e. with a dash of (affected) stupidity .

subabsurdus.definition: sub-absurdus adj., rather inappropriate, somewhat absurd: tempus discessūs.—Plur n. as subst, sayings affecting stupidity.

subaccuso.definition: sub-accūsō —, —, āre, to blame somewhat, find a little fault with: meum discessum: Vestorium.

subactio.definition: subāctiō ōnis, f sub+1 AG-, a thorough working ; of the mind, discipline .

subadroganter.definition: sub-adroganter adv., somewhat proudly, not without arrogance: facere.

subagrestis.definition: sub-agrestis e, adj., somewhat rustic, a trifle boorish: consilium.

subalaris.definition: subālāris e, adj. sub+ala, under the arms, carried under the arm : telum, N.

subamarus.definition: sub-amārus adj., slightly bitter: aliqua res. —Plur n. as subst: alios subamara delectent.

subausculto.definition: sub-auscultō —, —, āre, to listen secretly. eavesdrop: subauscultando excipere voces: quae loquor.

subcenturio1.definition: sub-centuriō or succenturiō —, ātus, ā re, to admit to a vacancy in a centuria; hence, to put in another's place, station as a substitute: in insidiis subcenturiatus, i. e. as a reserve, T.

subcenturio2.definition: sub-centuriō or succenturiō ōnis, m an under office, subcenturion, L.

subcontumeliose.definition: sub-contumēliōsē (succ-) adv., with a suggestion of contumely: tractare.

subcrispus.definition: sub-crīspus (succ-) adj., somewhat curled, a little frizzled: capillus.

subdeficiens.definition: sub-dēficiēns entis, adj., a little faint, somewhat failing, Cu.

subdifficilis.definition: sub-difficilis e, adj., slightly puzzling, rather hard: quaestio.

subditivus.definition: subditīvus adj. subdo, substituted, suppositious, spurious : archipirata.

subdo.definition: sub-dō didī, ditus, ere, to put under, set to, apply: ignem: calcaria equo, L.: se aquis, plunge into, O.— Fig., to bring on, furnish, supply, yield, afford: militum animis ignem, L.: alcui spiritūs, L.—To put in stea…

subdoceo.definition: sub-doceō —, —, ēre, to teach as a deputy school-master: meo labore subdoceri.

subdole.definition: subdolē adv. subdolus, cunningly, craftily : nihil subdole: speculatum Bocchi consilia, S.

subdolus.definition: sub-dolus adj., crafty, cunning, sly, subtle, deceptive, deceitful: animus, S.: oratio, Cs.: lingua, O.: loci forma, Ta.

subdubito.definition: sub-dubitō —, —, āre, to be somewhat in doubt, hesitate a little: antea: subdubitare te, quā essem voluntate.

subduco.definition: sub-dūcō dūxī (subdūxtī, T.), ductus, ere, to draw away, take away, lead away, carry off, wrest, withdraw, remove: lapidibus ex turri subductis, Cs.: rerum fundamenta: capiti ensem, V.: cibum athletae: Aenean manibus …

subductio.definition: subductiō ōnis, f subduco, a withdrawal, drawing up, hauling ashore : ad subductiones paulo facit humiliores (naves), Cs.—Fig., a reckoning .

subedo.definition: sub-edō ēdī, —, ere, to eat away below, wear away: scopulus, quā subederat unda, O.

subeo.definition: sub-eō iī (-īvit, O.; -īvimus, Ta.), itus, īre, to come under, go under, enter: in nemoris latebras, O.: cum luna sub orbem solis subisset, L.: tectum, i. e. enter a house, Cs.: Triviae lucos atque aurea tecta, V.: ca…

suber.definition: sūber eris, n the cork-oak, cork-tree: raptus de subere cortex, V.—Cork: silvestre, V.

subiacens.definition: sub-iacēns ntis, adj., lying beneath, subjacent, Cu.

subicio.definition: subiciō (the first syl. usu. long by position; often pronounced, and sometimes written, subiiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere sub+iacio, to throw under, place under, cast below : inter carros rotasque mataras subiciebant, disc…

subiecte.definition: (subiectē) adv. subiectus, humbly, submissively .— Only sup: haec subiectissime exponit, Cs.

subiectio.definition: subiectiō ōnis, f subicio, a putting under : rerum sub aspectum paene subiectio, i. e. a vivid presentation.—A substitution, forgery : testamentorum, L.

subiecto.definition: subiectō —, —, āre, freq. subicio, to throw under, place beneath, throw from below manūs, O.: lasso stimulos, H.: unda subiectat harenam, casts up , V.

subiector.definition: subiector ōris, m subicio, one who substitutes, a forger : testamentorum.

subiectus.definition: subiectus adj. with comp. P. of subicio, lying under, situated below, near, bordering upon, neighboring, adjacent : genae deinde ab inferiore parte tutantur subiectae: (cingulus terrae) subiectus aquiloni: Heraclea Ca…

subigito.definition: subigitō (subag-) —, —, āre sub+agito, to dishonor, lie with , T.

subigo.definition: subigō ēgī, āctus, ere sub+ago, to drive up, bring up : adverso flumine lembum Remigiis, i. e. drive up stream , V.: navīs subigi ad castellum iussit, L.— To turn up from beneath, break up, dig up, plough, cultivate, …

subinde.definition: sub-inde adv. —Of time, immediately after, just after, presently, forthwith, thereupon: primum gaudere, subinde, etc., H.: primus Aulus suppositus ac subinde Ostorius, Ta.: duae subinde urbes captae direptaeque, L.—Of…

subinsulsus.definition: sub-insulsus adj., somewhat tasteless, rather insipid.

subinvideo.definition: sub-invideō —, —, ēre, to be somewhat envious of: tibi.

subinvisus.definition: sub-invīsus adj., a little disliked, somewhat odious: apud malevolos nomen.

subinvito.definition: sub-invītō āvī, —, āre, to suggest to, invite by a hint: me, ut ad te scriberem.

subirascor.definition: sub-īrāscor ātus, ī, dep., to be out of temper, be somewhat provoked, be touched: interdum: brevitati litterarum: quod me non invitas.

subiratus.definition: sub-īrātus adj., somewhat angry: homo tibi: rescripsi tibi subiratus, with some feeling.

subitarius.definition: subitārius adj. subitus, in haste, sudden, hasty : aedificia, Ta.—Of troops, suddenly levied, raised for an emergency : milites, L.

subito.definition: subitō adv. subitus, suddenly, immediately, unexpectedly, at once, off-hand : subito tanta te impendent mala, T.: subito atque inproviso: ex oculis fugit, V.: nostras ad aurīs venire, O.: quod serenā nocte subito luna…

subitus.definition: subitus adj., sudden, unexpected, surprising: divortium: in rebus tam subitis: consilia, Cs.: novae rei ac subitae admiratio, L.: homo, rash.— As subst n., a sudden occurrence, surprise: subitum est ei remigrare: ad s…

subiungo.definition: sub-iungō iūnxī, iūnctus, ere, to fasten under, annex, attach: puppis rostro Phrygios subiuncta leones, having attached, V.—To yoke, harness: curru (dat.) tigrīs, V.—Fig., to bring under, subdue, subject, subjugate: u…

sublabor.definition: sub-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to glide under, slip away, sink: annis sublapsa vetustas, V.: retro sublapsa Spes Danaum, V.

sublate.definition: sublātē adv. with comp. sublatus, highly, loftily : dicere, with elevation : de me dixi sublatius, more arrogantly .

sublatio.definition: sublātiō ōnis, f sub+TAL-, an elevation, exaltation : animi.

sublatus.definition: sublātus adj. with comp. P. of tollo, elated, proud, haughty : animi, T.: quo proelio sublati Helvetii, Cs.: rebus secundis, V.: fidens magis et sublatior ardet, O.

sublego.definition: sub-legō lēgī, lēctus, ere, to gather from below, gather up: (puer) Sublegit quodcumque iaceret inutile, H.—To catch up secretly, gather by stealth: tibi carmina, V.—To choose as a substitute, elect instead: in demort…

sublevatio.definition: sublevātiō ōnis, f sublevo, an alleviation .

sublevo.definition: sub-levō āvī, ātus, āre, to lift from beneath, raise up, hold up, support: nos sibi ad pedes stratos: in ascensu sublevati, i. e. assisted, Cs.: alterni innixi sublevantesque invicem alii alios, L.: se, Cs.: terrā sub…

sublica.definition: sublica ae, f 2 LAC-, a stake, pile, palisade : sublicis in terram demissis, Cs.: isdem sublicis pontem reficere, piles , Cs.

sublicius.definition: sublicius adj. sublica, resting upon piles : Pons, the pile-bridge (across the Tiber), L.

subligaculum.definition: subligāculum ī, n subligo, a waist-band, breech-cloth .

subligar.definition: subligar āris, n 2 LIG-, a breech-cloth , Iu.

subligo.definition: sub-ligō —, —, āre, to bind below, bind on, fasten: lateri ensem, V.: clipeum sinistrae, V.

sublime.definition: sublīmē adv. with comp. sublimis, aloft, loftily, on high : Theodori nihil interest, humine an sublime putescat: elati, L.: sublimius altum Attollat caput, O.

sublimen.definition: sublīmen adv. cf. sublimis, on high, upwards : sublimen intro hunc rape, T.: aspice hoc sublimen candens, Enn. ap. C. (Ribbeck reads sublimen in several passages of Vergil, for sublime, etc.).

sublimis.definition: sublīmis e, adj. with comp. 2 LAC-, uplifted, high, lofty, exalted, elevated : vertex, V.: montis cacumen, O.: portae, V.: Os, uplifted (opp. pronus), O.: dum sublimis versūs ructatur, gazing upwards , H.: flagellum, …

sublimus.definition: sublīmus adj. old for sublimis, lofty, high : ex sublimo vertice, Acc. ap. C.

subluceo.definition: sub-lūceō —, —, ēre, to shine a little, gleam faintly, glimmer: aries sublucet corpore totus, C. poët.: sublucent crepuscula, O.: violae sublucet purpura nigrae, V.

subluo.definition: sub-luō —, lūtus, ere, to wash underneath, flow below, wash at the foot: montem flumen subluebat, Cs.: Asia, quā Hellesponto subluitur, Cu.

sublustris.definition: sublūstris e, adj. sub + * lustrus; LVC-, giving some light, faintly luminous, glimmering : nox, L., H.: umbra (noctis), twilight , V.

submergo.definition: sub-mergō (summ-) sī, sus, ere, to dip, plunge under, sink, overwhelm, submerge: submersus equus voraginibus: genera submersarum beluarum: navis submersa, Cs.: ferrum submersum in undā, O.: ipsos ponto, V.: procellis …

subministro.definition: sub-ministrō (summ-) āvī, ātus, āre, to aid by giving, give, furnish, afford, supply: tibi pecuniam: tela clam subministrantur: frumentum, Cs.

submisse.definition: submissē (summ-) adv. with comp. submissus.—Of manner, softly, gently, calmly, modestly : dicere: ornamentis uti summissius.— Of character, modestly, humbly, submissively : mihi supplicare: agere, O.: se gerere submis…

submissio.definition: submissiō (summ-) ōnis, f submitto, a letting down, lowering, dropping, sinking : vocis: nec elatio nec submissio, i. e. depression .

submissus.definition: submissus (summ-) adj. with comp. P. of submitto, let down, lowered, low : stantibus primis, secundis summissioribus, stooping lower , L.: Summisso humiles intrarunt vertice postīs, O.— Fig., of speech, low, soft, gen…

submitto.definition: sub-mittō (summ-) mīsī, missus, ere, to let down, put down, lower, sink, drop: se ad pedes, L.: latus in herbā , O.: poplitem in terrā, O.—Of animals, to keep for breeding, cause to breed: (pullos) in spem gentis, V.:…

submoleste.definition: submolestē (summ-) adv. submolestus, with some vexation : te non esse Romae submoleste fero, troubles me somewhat .

submolestus.definition: sub-molestus (summ-) adj., somewhat troublesome, rather vexatious: illud mihi.

submoneo.definition: sub-moneō (summ-) uī, —, ēre, to remind privily, hint: me, quod, etc., T.

submorosus.definition: sub-mōrōsus (summ-) adj., somewhat peevish, rather morose: quasi submorosa ridicula.

submoveo.definition: sub-moveō (summ-) mōvī (subj pluperf. summō sses, H.), mōtus, ēre, to put out of the way, drive back, drive off, send away, remove: hostīs ex mūro, Cs.: statione hostium lembos, L.: submotā contione, dismissed: submot…

submuto.definition: sub-mūtō (summūtō) —, — , āre, to interchange substitute: summutantur verba pro verbis.

subnascor.definition: sub-nāscor nātus, ī, dep., to grow up under, spring up afterwards, O.

subnecto.definition: sub-nectō —, xus, ere, to bind below, tie under, fasten beneath: subnectit fibula vestem, V.: antennis velum, O.: circlos Cervici, V.: mentum mitrā Subnexus, V.

subnego.definition: sub-negō —, āvī, āre, to deny in a measure, partly refuse: alqd praesenti tibi.

subnixus.definition: sub-nīxus (-nīsus) P., supported, propped, leaning, resting upon, sustained: (circuli) caeli verticibus subnixi: Parva Philoctetae subnixa Petelia muro, i. e. defended, V.—Fig., assured, confiding, relying, dependent:…

subnuba.definition: subnuba ae, f sub+NEB-, a rival : lecti nostri, O.

subnubilus.definition: sub-nūbilus adj., somewhat cloudy, overcast, obscure: nox, Cs.: Limes, O.

subo.definition: subō —, —, āre, to be lustful, H.

subobscenus.definition: sub-obscēnus (-caenus) adj., verging on indecency: ridiculum.

subobscurus.definition: sub-obscūrus adj., somewhat obscure, not very intelligible: breves et interdum subobscuri: ingressio.

suboffendo.definition: sub-offendō —, —, ere, to give some offence: apud faecem populi.

suboleo.definition: sub-oleō —, ēre, to emit a trifling smell.— With dat. of person, to be perceived, be suspected: Numquid subolet patri? T.

suboles.definition: subolēs (not sobo-), is, f sub+1 OL-, a sprout, shoot ; hence, fig., offspring, progeny, posterity, issue, stock, race, lineage : censores populi suboles, familias censento: propaganda (est tibi) suboles: priori Dissi…

subolesco.definition: sub-olēscō —, —, ere, inch, to grow up anew, arise instead: iuventus frequentior pro tot caesis exercitibus subolescens, L.

subolo.definition: subolō —, —, ere collat. form of suboleo, to be perceived, be suspected : Ut ne paululum quidem subolat, esse, etc., T.

suspicax.definition: suspicāx ācis, adj. suspicor, distrustful, suspicious : populus, N.: frater, L.

suspicio1.definition: suspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere sub+* specio; SPEC-, to look upwards, look up at : nec suspicit nec circumspicit: caelum: summum de gurgite caelum, O.: Quae tuam matrem (i. e. Pleiadem) tellus a parte sinistrā Suspicit, …

suspicio2.definition: suspīciō or suspītiō ō nis, f sub+ SPEC-, mistrust, distrust, suspicion : improborum facta suspitio insequitur: tanta nunc Suspitio de me incidit, T.: erat nemo, in quem ea suspitio conveniret: in suspitionem cadere: …

suspiciose.definition: suspīciōsē or suspītiosē adv. with comp. suspiciosus, in a suspicious manner, causing mistrust, suspiciously : quae argui suspitiose possunt, to excite distrust : suspitiosius dicere.

suspiciosus.definition: suspīciōsus or suspītiōsus adj. with sup. 2 suspicio, full of suspicion, mistrustful, ready to suspect, suspicious : an te conscientia suspitiosum faciebat?: civitas.— Causing mistrust, exciting suspicion, suspicious …

suspicor.definition: suspicor ātus, ārī, dep. SPEC-, to mistrust, suspect : ad suspicandum sagacissimus: fuge suspicari (sc. me), H.: quid homines suspicentur, videtis: debere se suspicari, Caesarem habere, etc., Cs.: venturos, Qui, etc.,…

suspiratus.definition: (suspīrātus, ūs) m suspiro, a sighing, sigh : suspiratibus haustis, O.

suspiritus.definition: (suspīritus, ūs) m suspiro, a deep breath, sigh .—Only abl sing. : quem nemo aspicere sine suspiritu posset: cum crebro suspiritu, L.

suspirium.definition: suspīrium ī, n cf. suspiro, a deep breath, sighing, sigh : si quis est sine suspirio: suspiria ducere, O.: Pectore repetens suspiria, O.

suspiro.definition: suspīrō āvī, ātus, āre sub+spiro, to draw a deep breath, heave a sigh, sigh : occulte: familiariter: ab imis Pectoribus, O.: solam in illam, O.: curae suspirantes, sighing , Enn. ap. C.: virgo Suspiret, eheu! ne, etc.…

suspitio.definition: suspītiō, suspītiōsē, suspī tiōsus see suspici-.

susque.definition: sūsque dēque adv. subs (see sub)+que, de+que, both up and down ; hence: de Octavio susque deque, it is all one , i. e. is of no consequence .

sustentaculum.definition: sustentāculum ī, n sustento, a prop, stay, support , Ta.

sustentatio.definition: sustentātīō ōnis, f sustento, a deferring, delay, forbearance : mora et sustentatio.

sustento.definition: sustentō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. sustineo, to hold up, hold upright, uphold, support, prop, sustain : fratrem dextrā , V.: aegre seque et arma, Cu.—Fig., to keep up, uphold, sustain, maintain, cherish, support, bear, up…

sustineo.definition: sustineō tinuī, tentus, ēre subs (see sub)+ teneo, to hold up, hold upright, uphold, bear up, keep up, support, sustain : umeris bovem: arma membraque, L.: infirmos baculo artūs, O.: manibus clipeos, O.: lapis albus P…

sustollo.definition: sustollō —, —, ere subs (see sub)+tollo, to lift, raise up, raise : sustollunt vela rudentes, Ct.: ad aethera voltūs, O.

sustuli.definition: sustulī perf. of suffero and of tollo.

susurro.definition: susurrō —, —, āre 1 susurrus, to hum, buzz, murmur, mutter, whisper : susurrant (apes), V.: cum carā de te nutrice, O.: iam susurrari audio, Civem Atticam esse hanc, T.

susurrus1.definition: susurrus ī, m cf. suri/zw, a humming, murmuring, muttering, whispering : mulierculae: (saepes) levi somnum suadebit inire susurro (apum), V.: tenui iugulos aperire susurro, Iu.: Lenes susurri, H.: blandi, Pr.—Person.,…

susurrus2.definition: susurrus adj. 1 susurrus, muttering, whispering : lingua, O.

suta.definition: sūta ōrum, n P. plur. n. of suo, plates fastened together, mail : aerea, V.

sutilis.definition: sūtilis e, adj. suo, sewed together, fastened together : Balteus, V.: coronae, i. e. sewed on the philyrae , O.

sutor.definition: sūtor ōris, m suo, a shoemaker, cobbler : id sutores conclamarunt, i. e. the vulgar , Iu.

sutorius.definition: sūtōrius adj. sutor, of a shoemaker, of a cobbler : atramentum, shoemakers' blacking : Turpio, once a shoemaker .

sutrinus.definition: sūtrīnus adj. sūtor, of shoemakers : taberna, Ta.

sutura.definition: sūtūra ae, f suo, a sewing together, seam, suture : scutale crebris suturis duratum, L.

suus.definition: suus (suae, monosyl., T.; gen plur. suūm, T.), pron poss. 3d pers. cf. sui, e(/os. I. In gen. A. With reflex reference, of oneself, belonging to oneself, his own, her own, his, her, its, their .—Referring to a subst. …

sycophanta.definition: sȳcophanta (sūc-) ae, m , sukofa/nths (prop., an informer against exporters of figs from Attica), an informer, tale-bearer, backbiter, slanderer: clamitent Me sycophantam, T.

syllaba.definition: syllaba (sul-) ae, f , sullabh/, a syllable: syllabarum numerus: longa, H.: brevis, O.: auceps syllabarum, i. e. a caviller.

syllabatim.definition: syllabātim adv. syllaba, syllable by syllable, by syllables : dictare.

symbola.definition: symbola (sumb-) ae, f , sumbolh/, a contribution to a feast, share, scot, shot: sumbolam dare, T.: ut de sumbolis essemus, T.

symphonia.definition: symphōnia ae, f , sumfwni/a, an agreement of sounds, concord, harmony, symphony: cum symphonia caneret: cantus symphoniae, L.: discors, H.: symphonias iactare.

symphoniacus.definition: symphōniacus adj. , sumfwniako/s, of con- certs, of music: pueri, choristers: servi.—Plur m. as subst, musicians.

synedrus.definition: synedrus ī, m , su/nedros, in Macedon, an assessor, counsellor, senator, L.

syngrapha.definition: syngrapha ae, f , suggrafh/, a written promise to pay, promissory note, bond: ex syngraphā agere.

synodus.definition: synodūs ontis, m , suno/dous, a bream (a sea-fish), O.

syrma.definition: syrma atis, n , su/rma, a robe with a train, tragic robe (to add to the actor's apparent stature), Iu.: quamquam omnia Syrmata volvas, i. e. tragic themes, tragedy, Iu.
